M1.reason: Against the brief's words the outline reads as a pump-action combat shotgun: a long barrel, a black receiver, a wooden pump under the barrel, and a stock at the far end. In the sides and top views the stock ends in a hook (the black hooked tip in top and below), and nothing sticks out or is missing.

M2.reason: The brief asks for about 30 long; the measured length is 29.3 (sizeOff 0.023), well inside 15%.

M3.reason: Named parts all present: the wooden pump on the barrel (top and left views), the black receiver, the black barrel with a muzzle, the wooden stock, and the hook at the stock's end (top view bottom, below view top). A grip and a small trigger loop also show. No folding hinge is plainly visible, but the line-up's Valve guns show no hinge either, so it is not charged.

M4.reason: Black metal for the barrel and receiver and a wooden tan for the pump and stock, which is what the brief asks for. The wood and the black are in the same places in every view.

M5.reason: The brief names no markings, panel lines or lettering. The wood grain on the pump and stock is visible at a similar sharpness, and the plain receiver adds nothing wrong.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test. In the four readings the asset was never picked as the one not made by Valve; the judges picked the other models (D, C, C, D), which is what chance gives.

M7.reason: The w_ model lies along its length in the side and top views, with the stock and muzzle at opposite ends. It is upright and sits on its origin as a dropped world weapon does.

M8.reason: The triangle count is 156, against a median of 138 and a third-quartile of 187 for Half-Life's own of its kind (the limit is twice the median, 276). The views show no open or inside-out faces, and the check passes.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the asset sits low on the view with the grip in the orange hand, the barrel pointing up and left, the same way round and held the same way as the game's own.
